news.title: Chelsea fans divided on Enzo Fernandez during first appearance since World Cup and transfer deadline
news.lede: The Argentine was handed his first pre-season minutes in Saturday’s 3-1 win over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge. Fans made their feelings clear when he replaced Reece James in the 62nd minute of the game. As his name was read out over the public address system, a chorus of boos were heard coming from the stands. Some fans opted to give Fernandez their backing by cheering the star as he stood on the touchline.

news.title: World Cup star Zion Suzuki in advanced talks over Premier League transfer as PSG move collapses
news.lede: The Villans' pursuit of Suzuki comes as Juventus revived their interest in Emi Martinez. Suzuki was poised to join European champions Paris Saint-Germain, who beat Villa 2-1 in the Super Cup on Wednesday. PSG and Parma had reached an agreement of approximately £29million for Suzuki, only for the deal to collapse on Saturday. It is understood a change in commissions surrounding the deal prompted PSG to withdraw.

news.title: Gianni Infantino threatened with Club World Cup boycott by powerful domestic football body
news.lede: A letter, signed by EFC CEO Charlie Marshall, was sent to FIFA General Secretary Mattias Grafström on July 31 just hours before Infantino's controversial plans to privatise FIFA were shelved. The news was first reported by The Guardian. talkSPORT previously revealed UEFA President Aleksander Čeferin was pushing for a Club World Cup boycott. UEFA's threat to not participate in FIFA tournaments remains in place and Ceferin wants the EFC to support this until Infantino resigns or removes himself from re-election next March.

news.title: Spain's FIFA World Cup final hero Ferran Torres leaves Barcelona for new challenge in France
news.lede: Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain have strengthened their already powerful attack by signing Spain star Ferran Torres from Barcelona on a five-year contract.PSG confirmed the transfer on Saturday but did not reveal the fee. French sports newspaper L’Equipe reported that the club paid around 50 million euros ($58 million) for the 26-year-old forward, who will wear the No. 9 shirt.Torres’ big move to PSGTorres became a World Cup hero after scoring Spain’s winning goal in extra time of the final against Argentina. Coming on as a substitute, he reacted quickly to a loose ball and fired a left-footed shot into the net.Reflecting on the goal, Torres said it was “scored by 47 million people,” referring to Spain’s population.The PSG move is the second major transfer of Torres’ career. Barcelona signed him from Manchester City in January 2022 for a reported 55 million euros.
